Proposition
[Connected Riemannian Manifolds Are $C^1$-Path Connected]

↗ def:riemannian-distance ↗ prop:riemannian-distance-finite

Any two points of a connected Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ can be joined by a $C^1$ curve $[0,1]\to M$. This is the $C^1$ form of Proposition 15 relative to Definition 15; existence of a metric on a smooth manifold follows from Proposition 2.
Proof

↗ def:riemannian-distance ↗ prop:riemannian-distance-finite \sketch By Proposition 15, $d_g(p,q)<d_g(p,q)+1<\infty $. Definition 15 then supplies a $C^1$ competitor from $p$ to $q$ of length below $d_g(p,q)+1$.

□
